plan.name: Retry briefly unavailable agent providers
plan.summary: Every Codex and Claude Code run used for drafting statements, planning, building or reviewing retries a terminal provider capacity, rate-limit, overload or dropped-connection error in the same workspace with the same job and agent, for at most three attempts with waits of five and ten seconds. Each wait releases both Codex turn locks, observes cancellation, and counts against one deadline that starts at the first attempt's turn and also covers reacquiring the turn; ordinary errors, successful runs and the existing thinking-loop fallback keep their present behavior. Exhaustion fails the step even if an interrupted attempt left usable files or passing checks, and the failure post retains that the provider was unavailable and the last provider error, including after saving and loading a build result. Update SPEC.md and README.md with the retry limits, released turns, timeout accounting and retryable failure explanation, citing D-0069, D-0125, D-0138, D-0154 and D-0122 in the affected SPEC bullets. The merger must record the new provider-retry decision, including its refinement of D-0154's timeout rule, because a plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestCodexRetriesCapacityWithTheSameJob
tests.says: A Codex build that stops at capacity waits five seconds and succeeds on its next attempt, keeping its workspace, prompt, permissions, tools, model, effort and transcript without taking a thinking-loop fallback.

tests.name: TestCodexRetriesRateLimitsAndDroppedConnections
tests.says: Codex retries terminal rate limits, dropped connections, an error event without a result, and provider errors reported on stderr.

tests.name: TestClaudeRetriesOverloadAndRateLimits
tests.says: Claude Code retries overloaded and rate-limit errors from result and assistant error events, and a dropped provider connection reported on stderr.

tests.name: TestProviderRetriesAreBoundedAndKeepTheLastError
tests.says: Each provider stops after three unsuccessful attempts with waits of five and ten seconds, saying it was unavailable and preserving the last provider error.

tests.name: TestProviderRetriesStopAtOrdinaryFailures
tests.says: A temporary provider failure is retried, but an ordinary failure stops immediately even after a retry; successful output and tool failures that mention provider errors cause no retry.

tests.name: TestProviderWaitCountsAgainstTheRunTimeout
tests.says: Both providers stop when the original job deadline expires during backoff, retaining the provider error and deadline cause without launching another attempt.

tests.name: TestProviderRetriesKeepTheOriginalDeadline
tests.says: A second failed attempt does not renew the job's time limit; its last error survives expiration during the second wait.

tests.name: TestCodexReleasesBothTurnsDuringProviderWait
tests.says: While a Codex run waits to retry, another step using the same sign-in takes the process turn and the home file lock and finishes before the waiting run resumes.

tests.name: TestCancellingAProviderWaitStopsRetries
tests.says: Cancellation interrupts a pending provider wait promptly and prevents another attempt.

tests.name: TestCodexRetryTurnWaitKeepsTheDeadline
tests.says: Time spent reacquiring the Codex turn after backoff counts against the original deadline, and its expiry leaves the other step running.

tests.name: TestProviderFailureIsPostedAfterSavingTheBuild
tests.says: A failure post made from a saved modeled build retains provider unavailability, the last error and the retry instruction even when a final gate report exists.

tests.name: TestProviderExhaustionCannotPublishAPassingBuild
tests.says: An exhausted provider leaves a modeled build failed and needing a person even if its leftover code passes the final gate.

tests.name: TestEveryDraftReportsProviderExhaustionDespiteLeftoverFiles
tests.says: Statement drafts, plumbing plans and plans of issues report provider exhaustion instead of proposing files left by an interrupted attempt.

tests.name: TestPlumbingBuildFailsWhenItsProviderNeverFinishes
tests.says: A plumbing build whose provider never finishes fails with the provider error even if its leftover files pass the checks, and it neither reviews nor takes a thinking-loop fallback.

tests.name: TestPlumbingReviewsRetryAndReportProviderExhaustion
tests.says: The separate review run retries a temporary provider failure and can approve after recovery; when its time budget expires instead, it does not approve and retains the provider diagnostic.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and 15 acceptance tests covering provider retries, deadlines, turn sharing, failure reports, and documentation updates. Check 1 passed: every acceptance test fails on the base code, and `repo/` is unchanged.
